rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a conditional branch sends a request to another party and that the process continues only after that party's response, with the response then leading on to the activity that follows the branch: When a conditional split leads to a request and a later response, model the response as an activity that receives its own incoming sequence flow from the split and sends a sequence flow onward to the merge point where the unconditional path rejoins. Join the no-issue path and the response path with a gateway before the next activity, so that no response activity forms a separate start-to-end chain.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a conditional branch sends a request to another party and that the process continues only after that party's response, with the response then leading on to the activity that follows the branch

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that the whole process is then closed as a final action, after an ordered sequence of earlier steps has finished (for example 'the entire process is then closed'): Model the stated closing action as its own bpmn:task placed after the last preceding step and before the final end event, labeled with the action the description gives. Do not replace it with an end event alone, and do not drop it or fold it into the label of an earlier task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that the whole process is then closed as a final action, after an ordered sequence of earlier steps has finished (for example 'the entire process is then closed')

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a reviewer may either approve an item or send it back for rework, and the send-back branch is followed by a further action and then by a resubmission for another review of the same item: Place an exclusive gateway at the decision point, with one outgoing branch per outcome the description names. On the approval branch, model the approval as its own task on the item. On the send-back branch, model the return action the description names as its own task, then model the rework as a separate task, then model the resubmission as its own task that leads back to the same review step. Do not merge the return action and the rework into one task, and do not label the rework task with the name of the return action.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a reviewer may either approve an item or send it back for rework, and the send-back branch is followed by a further action and then by a resubmission for another review of the same item

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the process begins when a participant performs an action (for example, filling in information or signing up) that is followed by further system activity: Model the process start as a plain start event, then model the participant's described action as a task placed after it and before the next system activity. Do not use the action as the label of the start event.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the process is started by a participant that first performs a stated action of its own, such as dispatching a communication to another party, and further work follows that action

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a set of activities can be done in any order but all of them must be completed before the process continues: Model each activity in that set as its own task. Place these tasks between a parallel split gateway and a parallel join gateway, so that all branches start and the join waits for all of them before the next step. Do not place an exclusive gateway or any decision condition among these branches, and do not use a single task or a subprocess to stand for the set.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a set of activities can be done in any order but all of them must be completed before the process continues

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a conditional branch starts a named activity, and the steps it involves are described as its contents rather than as steps of the main flow: Model the named activity as a single task on that conditional branch, connected by sequence flows to the surrounding gateways. Do not replace it with an embedded subprocess that has its own start and end events, and do not lift its listed contents into the main flow as separate branches unless the description sequences them as main steps.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a conditional branch starts a named activity, and the steps it involves are described as its contents rather than as steps of the main flow

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a conditional branch launches an action and then lists that action's parts (such as analysis, interviews or visits), with no separate nested workflow of its own described: Model the launched action as a single task on the main flow, placed after the branch's conditional gateway, and model its listed parts as tasks or gateways in the main flow where the description orders them. Do not model the launched action as an embedded subprocess with its own start and end events.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a conditional branch launches an action and then lists that action's parts (such as analysis, interviews or visits), with no separate nested workflow of its own described
